title: On the computational cost of Stochastic Gradient Langevin Dynamics
summary: Stochastic Gradient Langevin Dynamics (SGLD) reduces the cost of Langevin-based sampling by replacing full-dataset drift evaluations with mini-batch approximations, but the resulting subsampling error may offset this computational saving. We study this trade-off for stochastic differential equations with finite-sum drifts and compare the computational cost of SGLD with that of the Euler-Maruyama (EM) method. For a prescribed mean-square accuracy $\varepsilon^2$, we derive complexity estimates that explicitly track the dependence on the dataset size $m$, mini-batch size $s$, and accuracy…
